Subject: Acme | Rerank model fit validation — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Samira / Ben,

Thanks again for the call today — good discussion on where reranking sits in your search stack and the key quality metrics you care about. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move to a short pilot.

Call highlights:
- Scope: POC on product search reranking for web + mobile (product detail and query rewriting out of scope for now).
- Success metrics: primary = NDCG@10 (weighted by conversions), secondary = MRR for navigation queries.
- Baseline: your current in-house reranker (TF-IDF+BM25+light learning-to-rank) — sample baseline numbers we captured in the call.
- Risk: potential quality regressions on long-tail sparse queries; will need promptset coverage for those segments.

Recommended initial model fit and eval plan (attached):
1) Eval set: 10k queries sampled from last 90 days (we included the promptset file).
2) Models to validate: redwood-rerank-large-3 (default), redwood-rerank-medium-2 (lower latency), Llama2-70B-q4f16 (open baseline).
3) Metrics: NDCG@1/3/10, MRR, and per-query click-through delta.
4) Safety/QA: run your top-1000 SKU blacklists through the reranker and verify no regression.

Quick results (see attached spreadsheet for full breakdown):
- redwood-rerank-large-3: NDCG@10 = 0.612 (+0.078 vs baseline), MRR = 0.421 (+0.045)
- redwood-rerank-medium-2: NDCG@10 = 0.596 (+0.062 vs baseline), MRR = 0.409 (+0.033)
- Llama2-70B-q4f16: NDCG@10 = 0.575 (+0.041 vs baseline), MRR = 0.392 (+0.016)

Notes & concerns:
- Long-tail drop: a subset (~8% of eval queries) shows non-trivial NDCG variance; we should expand the promptset for those segments before a full rollout.
- Latency: large model adds ~45ms median to your request path under current infra; medium model is ~22ms. We can apply batching/quantization recommendations in Redwood Optimize to reduce this.

Proposed A/B pilot (2 weeks):
- 10% traffic to redwood-rerank-medium-2, 10% to redwood-rerank-large-3, 80% control.
- Collect NDCG & MRR daily, monitor CTR and conversion. Failure criteria: sustained drop >2% conversion or NDCG regression >0.03 at cohort level.

Next steps / asks from Acme:
- Sign off on the attached mutual action plan (MAP) so we can kick off data ingest and evaluation.
- Confirm which dataset slice you want prioritized for long-tail coverage (mobile nav vs web discovery).

Attachments:
- 20260824-acme-rerank-results.xlsx (detailed metric breakdown)
- acme-rerank-promptset-v1.jsonl (sample promptset)
- acme-mutual-action-plan.pdf (MAP)

Thanks — I can schedule the pilot kickoff as soon as I have sign-off on the MAP and a technical contact for data ingest.

FYI — attaching the detailed XLSX with per-query examples and a short long-tail sample set (anonymized IDs). Below is a quick technical clarification on Samira's questions.

On Tue, 25 Aug 2026 at 09:40 AM Samira Khan <samira@acme.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — this is really helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we sign the MAP:
>
> 1) On the NDCG deltas you listed: are those computed on click-weighted labels or the raw relevance judgments? We want the evaluation to reflect our conversion-weighted business metric.
> 2) For the long-tail 8% you flagged, can you share examples (anonymized) so our search team can verify coverage?
> 3) Timeline: if we sign today, how quickly can you start the pilot? We need an estimate for procurement (SOW) planning.

Answers: 
- NDCG numbers in the spreadsheet are click-weighted by default (we used your provided event feed). We also included raw-judgment NDCG in a second tab.
- Long-tail sample: see sheet 'long_tail_examples' — 800 anonymized query IDs and 120 example query texts (anonymized). This should surface the coverage gaps.
- Pilot start: once MAP is signed and we have a secure S3 ingest endpoint with 7 days of data transfer, we can run the offline eval and spin up the pilot in ~10 business days. If you need faster, we can reduce the dataset to a 3-day slice for a quicker smoke test (5 business days).

Performance note: large model adds ~45ms median; if latency is a hard cap we recommend starting with redwood-rerank-medium-2 in pilot and collecting quality telemetry. We can also enable per-request async reranking (non-blocking) to hide latency during the pilot if that fits your UX.
